utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yesterday the Defence made an application for the admission of some hospital records. The Trial Chamber had the records marked for identification and stated that it would give a decision on their admission today. I do so now. If the Defence wish to call evidence on Pionirska Street, they may do so when they present their case, and at that time they of course may present any evidence relating to Pionirska, including that of Mr. Vasiljevic and the hospital records. Those witnesses would then be open to cross-examination by all the parties, and this answers the point raised by Mr. Cepic yesterday. The hospital records, therefore, remain marked for identification. Would you call the next witness, Mr. Groome. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your permission may I take this unique opportunity while Mr. Vasiljevic is still in this court and for the economy of time I'd like you to give me permission to ask Mr. Vasiljevic two or three questions which stem from document P97 and its link to the Lukic family, and that would -- and then we wouldn't have to recall him during the Defence case and have all the costs and expenditure incurred then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, we're going to allow it, but confine it to this request that you made, that is questions relating to the Lukic family, which did arise yesterday. If you seek to go beyond that, then that falls within the parameters of the ruling that I just gave. You would then have to call your own witness. But I'm not certain whether he's immediately available. Mr. Alarid?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I was actually going to speak on an unrelated matter, Your Honour, given the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay. Let us conclude this first.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let me hear from the court deputy about the availability.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: He's expected in 30 minutes, so we'll start the other witness, then, yes. And now Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do want to raise just some overall general concerns with the Chamber with regards to sort of how the trial is progressing as well as sort of the way this trial is manifesting in motion, yet we're still doing a large amount of preparation. The OTP has had eight filings this week. Three of the motions came with over a hundred pages and are deadlines to file responses to these and what's most prejudicial, Your Honour, is these motions involve the addition of nine new witnesses, changes on the witness list, things like that. We're really having a hard time keeping up at this point considering the voluminous nature of the filings, the addition of new information, the constant disclosure of new information that involves mostly B/C/S and untranslated materials, and we really feel that at this juncture there is a real threat of prejudice to the Defence considering the way the pace of the trial is actually very fast combined with the fact that we're still having to deal with I think what are essentially pre-trial issues during the trial, and we were wondering if the Court would entertain a one-week recess so we can -- so we can answer all these. I mean a lot these are going to come due at the end of next week considering the two-week deadline for ordinary filings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But this overlaps with a motion that is in front of me from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: To amend the trial sitting schedule so that we would sit for four days.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I'm trying to find a solution, Your Honour, to our --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, let us see if we can find a solution to that, because that may resolve if not wholly, then partially the problem you have. I'm to ask the Prosecutor how he responds to the motion for trial sittings of four days a week.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecutor is preparing a written response that we intended to file today, but I can certainly address it now, and I guess one of the suggestions that I might put forward is that some of these motions, it may be more expedient and may involve less time of -- less of Mr. Alarid's time, some of these motions might be able to be dealt with in oral argument, taking five minutes to discuss the issues, present the positions to the -- Your Honours, and then it could be decided sometime afterwards. So that might save some time and ease the burden on Mr. Alarid if the Court wants to consider that. With respect to Mr. Alarid's motion, we are of course endeavouring to comply with it -- the Chamber's rulings in the Pre-Trial Chamber. We anticipate that we will be able to although there are some difficulties. With respect to whether the trial schedule should be reduced to four days, I feel that's a matter for the Chamber's discretion. I don't have any personal knowledge of the workload of the Defence so I wouldn't want to comment on it. So all I would say is that we're prepared to go forward with the schedule, but we will trust in the Chamber's discretion on what it deems is the fairest way to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we agree that there's a fast tempo for these proceedings, and we have nothing against the request, and it is a privilege on behalf of Mr. Domazet to be able to address this Trial Chamber. I think he'll be able to tell you more. He's catching a plane, and he considers that his presence here is not absolutely necessary. So could you give Mr. Domazet a chance to address the Trial Chamber, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, but to address me on what? If he wishes to leave, he may leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. [In English] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, your mike.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: At the end of the first break or the beginning of the second session we'll give a decision on the Defence application for a four-day sitting. Call the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, just prior to calling the witness, if you recall the Chamber also deferred to today its decision on certain excerpts from section 3 of Prosecution Exhibit 96, that is to do with the paramilitary groups. I'll just remind the Chamber of that. Maybe perhaps sometime today we could come back to that. The specific clips that I'm seeking -- or that I'm suggesting were implicated during the cross-examination were clips 29, 32, 34, and 36. And, Your Honour, the Prosecution's next witness will be led by -- or questioned by Mr. Ossogo, and it's VG-58.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll give a ruling on your application relating to the clips later today. Did I see the hand of Mr. Lukic, Milan Lukic? What is it that you wish to say? THE ACCUSED M. LUKIC: [Interpretation] Yes. I would like to ask the Trial Chamber because this is a protected witness, and Mr. Domazet has nothing to do with the next witness, that he leave the courtroom or I'll leave the courtroom. The next witness is coming in. Domazet isn't his counsel, so I don't see the purpose for his remaining in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: This is rather strange. You're making a request for Mr. Domazet to leave the courtroom? You have become a counsel? THE ACCUSED M. LUKIC: [Interpretation] If he's not a counsel for the next witness and if he's not my Defence counsel, I don't see the purpose of him remaining in the courtroom if the witness coming is indeed a protected witness. I apologise, but that's what I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, who requires Mr. Domazet to stay? I don't require him to stay. I've told him he can leave. He's perfectly free to leave. Nothing that I've said indicates [Realtime transcript read in error "entitles"] that he should stay. It's entirely a matter for him. Mr. Domazet, very quickly. MR. DOMAZET [Interpretation] Your Honour, as quick as I can. I've been informed that Mr. Vasiljevic will be here again and that my presence is necessary, so I have a plane ticket this evening instead of Saturday and I'm due to leave. Now, in view of the present situation and the fact that Mr. Vasiljevic will be just asked a few questions, I really don't see the need for me to be present. You can go ahead without me. So I was just going to request that I be allowed to leave the courtroom so that there's no need for a reaction of this kind on the part of Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. You are excused if you wish, Mr. Domazet. Let us get on with the work of the trial. Call the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG-58, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just to be clear, I have just seen the transcript and me saying nothing I have said entitles him to say. It's the exact opposite. I said nothing I have said requires him to stay. Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit, and you may begin, Mr. Ossogo. Before you begin, though, I'm feeling rather hot in this courtroom and I have to ask that something be done about it. Yes. I've been told that they have been advised that it is unduly hot. Yes, Mr. Ossogo.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. The Prosecution calls Witness VG-58. I'm going to submit witness -- to Witness VG-58 a pseudonym sheet through the usher, because we're dealing here with a protected witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Witness VG-58, the usher is currently showing you a pseudonym sheet. On this pseudonym sheet can you confirm that you can find your first name, last name, and your date of birth? Are these -- is this information correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Please sign at the bottom of the pseudonym sheet with the pen that the usher is handing out to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Witness VG-58, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Madam Usher. Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Please take a look at the back of the pseudonym sheet, and here you will find a name and a pseudonym, and you may have to use the pseudonym if you want to refer to that person during your testimony. Please use the pseudonym of that person during the testimony in case you need to mention that person.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Prosecution would like to tender the pseudonym sheet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is admitted as P98 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'd like us to move briefly into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Witness VG-58, could you tell us the circumstances surrounding your meeting with these White Eagles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: I met them on the Drina Bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: They speak to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: They said that we should go back home and that we should not linger there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Did they check your ID, either your own or the people who were with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes. They checked my ID as well as my husband's.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: You were with your husband. Were you with other people also?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: My children were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Since this Mr. Momir Mioskovic was your neighbour, did you ever see White Eagles in his house at one point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: I saw outside the door, beneath the vine there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: What were they doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: They were sitting there on several occasions drinking.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: They were wearing weapons -- carrying weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: How were they dressed? Did they have uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: They were in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Could you describe these uniforms for us, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes, I can. These were camouflage uniforms. They had caps on their shoulders.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: What colour were these uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: They were military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Among these White Eagles were you able to recognise anyone at one point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Give us the names of the people you recognised.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Milan Lukic, Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Did you know Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Mitar Vasiljevic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: How did you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: I knew him because he worked at the Hotel Panos.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Did you go to this Hotel Panos?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Did Mitar Vasiljevic ever enter into your own house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: What did you do when he arrived into your house, and why did he -- why had he come?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: He was looking for gold -- or, rather, first he asked us to turn over a rifle, then he asked for gold, and when we had none of that, he asked for money.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Was he alone or were there other people with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes, there was Milan Lukic, Sredoje Lukic, and Jovisa Planojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: These people you just mentioned, Sredoje Lukic, Milan Lukic, and Jovisa Planojevic, did they -- did you open the door for them, or did they break into the house or enter in another way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes. Mitar kicked the door in.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Were you alone in your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: I was there with my two children.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: You told us about gold. Did you give them what they wanted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Later on after this incident, after the fact that this group broke into your house, what did you do with your children? Did you leave the house or did you stay in the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: He told us that we should wait for him there, that he would kill my children unless we stayed there waiting for him. However, he never showed up at the house any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Was your husband with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Were you afraid?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Did you hide?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Throughout at that time I never dared to enter my home. I once did, and I found that a bag of flour had been thrown on the floor, and some of my belongings were strewn around, and that was the last time I went into my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: I will now like to talk about Sadija Dedic, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please move into private session?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Witness VG-58, did you know Sadija Dedic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: I did. I'd often go to her place for a cup of coffee.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Where did she live?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: She lived at Seganje next to Momir Mioskovic. First there was Ibrahim Dedic's house then Sadija Dedic and then Rasim Dedic's house. They were all in one courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Did you know her husband?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes, Latif.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: You're mentioning Latif. That was her husband's name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Did you know what happened to Sadija Dedic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: It was like this: It was sometime around 9.00 or half past 9.00, (redacted) There's a shed up by the road and then there's an iron gate, and there's some concrete there and steps and an entrance, and I heard and saw the gate opening. It was roughly opened, and they entered the house. There were four or five of them. I didn't count them properly because it was dark. I recognised Milan Lukic there, Sredoje Lukic, Jovisa Planojevic, Mitar Vasiljevic. And there was someone else there, but I wasn't able to recognise them. They entered the house, and they asked Sadija for her valuables. However, while they were opening the door Latif escaped to the bathroom. There's a bathroom on the right-hand side, and he jumped out of the window, and they kept asking Sadija for money and for her valuables, her gold. She gave what she had and said she had nothing else, but they kept asking her for more. There was a lot of commotion, a lot of noise, and I saw -- well, it went on for quite a long -- well, there was a burst of gunfire shortly afterwards, and then they left. The door banged shut, and the car door was slammed, and they went off towards the bus station and the centre of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that you heard shots. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: That's right. I was not even a metre away from the house. I was in the Sadija Dedic courtyard. Sadija Dedic's courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Did you recognise the person who shot that burst of gunfire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Who was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Could you tell us how he was dressed when he did this, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes, I can do that. He was wearing a black -- black overalls, and on his head he had a sort of sock. You could just see his eyes. And he had gloves on too. And he had a rifle on him, the short one.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: You're saying that he had some kind of sort of sock on his head? So how were you able to identify him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: I recognised his voice, because he was the one screaming at Sadija most. He shouted out "Not Rozaje. He's not in Rozaje. Give me some more gold and money."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Apart from this voice that you heard and that you recognised as being Milan Lukic's, are there other features that really struck you and that could really support the fact that you recognised Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: I'm sure I recognised him. You know what? Let me put it this way, let me tell you this way. Your Honours, he went with Behija Biscanka's car, in her car, and he was the only person who drove that car.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: You are saying that he was driving Behija's car. What make was this car, and what colour was this car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: A Passat, red in colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Were there any other colours of the same make around and the same colour in Visegrad or any other -- that you could have seen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Is this a new car or a secondhand car or an old car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: It was a new car.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: You said that this car belonged to a lady called Behija. Did you know this lady?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: How did you know her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: She had a shop by the bridge, and I would meet her there quite often, and that's how I knew her. The Rzava bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Did you know how this car ended up in Milan Lukic's hands, who was driving it since it used to belong to this lady Behija?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I did know that, because the woman was very rich. She lived a comfortable life, and I heard that Milan Lukic killed her. And he was the only one who drove that car. Nobody else drove it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Let's return to what happened in the Dedic household. You said that Mr. Dedic escaped through a window?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ossogo.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How long did you plan to spend on this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we plan on about two hours. A viva voce witness, as you see, and we had earmarked about two hours for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: As they say in track and field athletics, you must pick up the pace.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'll try to be like Husain Bolt, just as fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Perhaps faster.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Witness VG-58, could you tell us whether Mr. Dedic came back after he escaped his house and after his wife was murdered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: He came in the morning. Well, I entered the house first and then he came.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: What happened to Sadija's body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: When I went into the house I saw her turned this way. She had turned herself around, and her brain was spattered all over the house. By the door there was a hole this big from the impact from when the rifle hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to talk about Rasim Dedic. Did you know Rasim Dedic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes, I did know him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We need to go back to public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was about to ask for it. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to Mr. Rasim Dedic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I don't remember what day it was, but it was 1.00 in the afternoon. They killed him in his own house.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Do you remember the year this happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: I can't remember what year it was or the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Was it after Sadija was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Three days after Sadija.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: And Sadija Dedic was killed after he had moved to Seganje, is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Reformulate.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Witness VG-58, you said that Rasim Dedic's murder occurred a few days -- three days after Sadija Dedic was killed, after Sadija Dedic was killed. Do you remember when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes, three or four days. I can't remember exactly when. I think it was sometime in June anyway, but when exactly I really can't remember. I can't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Do you remember in what year this happened? You seem to remember the month. Could you please tell us the year it happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ossogo, you might consider that --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1992, in June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The incident of Rasim Dedic, which is not in the indictment, does not mean it's not relevant, it has its own relevance, but perhaps you can deal with matters like that very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely, but this witness needs to be told about the events along a time line in order to know what happened. Some other witnesses don't need this, but this witness needs to be told about the chronology of the event -- of the events, needs to be led in some way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Ossogo, it's time for the break. We'll take the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ossogo. Ever mindful, I hope, of the need to pick up the pace.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely, Your Honour. Yes, I'm mindful of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: VG-58, Witness VG-58, we are now going to deal with an incident that took place in the area of Bikavac. Do you remember the fire that happened in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Could you please describe the events for us. Could you tell us what you saw.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes. I was nearby, about five metres away, maybe even closer, and I'm going to describe where I was. It was towards evening. I don't know exactly what the time was. There were quite a lot of women there and children, too, young girls, not to enumerate them at all. They were at Meho Aljic's house, quite a lot of them. And then a red Passat turned up. Milan Lukic was there, Sredoje Lukic, too, Mitar Vasiljevic, Jovisa Planojevic, and there were some others, but I didn't know those others. They forced the people into Meho Aljic's house, and I saw it all. I saw them telling the people to go into the house. Milan Lukic said, "Come on. Let's get as many people in as possible," from Zupa, Gostilja, Velika and Mala, Zlijeb and so on, all these different places, but it's called Zupa, actually. And they forced all people into the house, and by that time it was already dark. From behind Meho Aljic's house I heard some banging like a hammer, a strong object, the banging noise, and the door shut suddenly. And then not 10 or 20 minutes later they got back into the car and left and the house burst into flames. They put some petrol on it, and I heard and saw that there were tracer bullets. They shot tracer bullets into the house. And anyway, it all caught fire and was set alight.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness VG-58. Let's return to the individuals you saw. You told us that you saw Milan Lukic, Sredoje Lukic, Mitar Vasiljevic, and Jovisa Planojevic. What was Milan Lukic doing exactly? What was his role within this group of people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: It was like this: He had a short rifle. I don't know what the name of that kind of rifle is, but anyway, he pushed the people into that house with that rifle and managed to do that. They all went into the house, and then they set fire to the house. And a little while after that, the car left and the house was ablaze. You could hear screams like the screams of cats. It was just terrible.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: What did Sredoje Lukic do, because you saw him as well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes, he was there too. He did the same. He was busy pushing the people into the house, all of them in that group. There were some other people, too, in that group of theirs, but I couldn't recognise the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I think that the previous question was leading question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: If it was, only marginally so. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Witness, you were describing what Sredoje Lukic was doing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: How was Milan Lukic dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: He had black overalls, one piece, black one-piece on him, and he had -- you know, what they put that -- the thing you put for the rifle, for putting the bullets into, and he had a knife and a short rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: What about Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: They were dressed the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: In your view, these two individuals you recognised amongst others where the house of Meho Aljic was on fire, were these two individuals the same as the one that you identified for the Chamber earlier on and are here with us in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I would object to the characterisation of identification. I don't believe there was an identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Proceed. That's a matter on which the Trial Chamber will make a determination as to the weight. Do you have the same point, Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your -- Your Honour, just to add something related to the previous identification, who's wearing the blue jacket and who's wearing the grey jacket, for the record. With your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You're asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No, no, just for the record, to put in the record, because the witness described one of the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm not going back to it. I've told counsel that he can come back to that. Let us be orderly.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: VG-58, did you get my question? Can you answer my question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Yes. I was asking you the following: During the fire at Bikavac you've just described, you identified Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic, among others. These two individuals, are they here in this courtroom today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: I'd like to return to something you said. You said that women and children were gathered together. You said that Milan Lukic brought all these people together, if I remember correctly. Were there also men within that group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "I did not see," said the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Could you give us a ballpark figure of the number of people being gathered in this group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Roughly over 60.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: You said that you were close by, that you were about five metres away from the house of Meho Aljic. Do you remember roughly where you were standing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Where were you in respect to the house of Mr. Meho Aljic? Were you behind the house, in front of the house, next to the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: In front of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Were you able to identify other houses nearby next to the house of Mr. Aljic, houses whose owners you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I know Dervo from Zlijeb, a house below the road. VG-114, Sumbula Pecikoza.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we move into private session for this part of my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Witness, I'm now going to show you a picture, and on that picture you will be able to show us the house where the fire took place, and you will be able to tell us as well where you were. I'm going to ask the registrar to display Exhibit 175.10 on the 65 ter list. It's part of exhibit -- or of 00175. Whilst the document is being brought up on our screens, I'd like, Witness VG-58, I'd like to ask you whether you were able to recognise anyone in that group of people that had been brought together.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Could you please give us the names of those whom you recognise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Meho Aljic's sister-in-law Suhra, with a baby; Tija Spoljan, her daughter-in-law with two children from -- then Tija Ceric's [phoen] daughter, and her daughter's daughter and a baby.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: You've just given us the names of a number of people you recognised and who were pushed into the house of Meho Aljic. We now have the photograph on our screens, but I don't think it's working properly. You mentioned VG-114. Was VG-114 amongst those people in that group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I object to the leading nature of the question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't see anything leading in that. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: You told us that the house burnt down. Could you tell us who set fire to the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Milan Lukic, Sredoje Lukic, Jovisa Planojevic, Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: How did they set fire to the house? What did they use to set fire to the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: They used petrol to light the fire, as well as bullets that were fired from a rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: You were in front of the house of Meho Aljic. Could you tell us how long it all lasted? You said that you heard screams for a while. How long did it last?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: It lasted perhaps half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: After this half hour could you still hear screams coming from the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: You said that there were children, young children, babies. Were you able to see how many babies there were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes. I wasn't able to see how many children there were, but there were many.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Thank you. There was this fire in this house, the fire you saw. Do you know what the perpetrators, Milan Lukic, Sredoje Lukic, Vasiljevic, do you know what they did afterwards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes. They took the car and got out of the driveway onto the street leading from Banpolje toward the town, toward the hotel in Bikavac. Milan Lukic took two girls and got them into a van. I wasn't able to see who was driving the van, but they drove them away toward the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: You said that they took a car. What colour was that car?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we just heard that witness mentioned just Milan Lukic and now in question we have plural.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's quite so, Mr. Ossogo. The previous evidence was that Milan Lukic took two girls and got them into a van. But then she said, but they drove them towards the town. So, Witness, how many persons took the two girls and put them into the van and drove them towards the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All of them were there. Nobody had left earlier or later. They got into the car. I wasn't able to see who was at the wheel. I was only able to see Milan Lukic forcing them onto a van.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Do you know who else got into the car? Did you see Milan Lukic go into the car? Did you see Milan Lukic go into the car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw him push them into a van. I saw him do that personally, but I don't know who the driver was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And do you know who else got into the car apart from the two girls?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Those who were part of the group did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And who was part of the group? Are you able to name them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Milan Lukic, Sredoje Lukic, Jovisa Planojevic, Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Witness VG-58, after these events, after the perpetrators had left, what did you do, because you were hiding in a place where you saw all these events. What did you do then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: I was there until VG-114 went past.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Was VG-114 alive? Did VG-114 survive the fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Do you know if other people survived this fire in Bikavac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in public session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Go ahead, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ms. VG-58, my name is Jason Alarid, and I'm counsel for Milan Lukic. May I ask you some questions today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, isn't it true that you lost or -- many family members in this war in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And for the first time in your statement in April of 2008 you mention the belief that your mother, as well as other family members, were in this house on Bikavac; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And at no time prior to April 2008 did you mention this suspicion that your mother and sisters were in this house in Bikavac. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: I didn't even mention my father. My father was detained in the school building on Pionirska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that after the war the names of Milan Lukic, Sredoje Lukic, and Mitar Vasiljevic were talked about amongst the refugees from Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: I don't know who talked about what. I only know who did what.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And it's because you're saying you're an eyewitness and recognise these gentlemen at many stages in your time in Visegrad. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, on the date of the Bikavac fire, you're indicated and you drew on the map that you were five metres from the fire the whole time. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't measure the distance, of course, but it was roughly that, and I swear to God. I'm not going to lie.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, just to let you know, the Prosecutor took 90 minutes in his examination-in-chief, and that's about the time that you will have as a maximum. Of course, you don't have to use it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll try not to.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'll try not to, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, during this time that you indicate that just Milan Lukic, Sredoje Lukic, Mitar Vasiljevic, and one other individual, Mr. Planojevic, was at the scene?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You didn't describe what Mitar Vasiljevic was wearing. What was he wearing? And how did you know who he was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: I know for sure. He wore the black overall. He had gloves on his hands, a rifle in his hands, a knife at his belt, a bullet belt across his chest and a cap on his head, something like a sock or stocking or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Was the stocking pulled down over his face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes, but you could see his eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so you know Mitar Vasiljevic enough that you would recognise him from his eyes alone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I can recognise him now too.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, I put to you that you were offered a photograph of Mitar Vasiljevic and you were not able to name him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: I recognised him. I'm not going to lie. I've come here to tell the truth. I'm not ashamed. So if I recognised somebody, I say so. And I'm not afraid of anyone either. I just fear God.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But in your statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ossogo.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the counsel could please specify when this photograph was shown to the witness - I believe that it was in the Vasiljevic case - so that the witness can locate herself in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: She seemed to have been aware of it, but, yes, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I put to you that it was attached to your 14, 15 of May, 2000, statement tendered to the OTP investigators. Do you recall giving this statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, before we move on to that statement, though, I would like to take your attention to April of this year where you filed clarifications to the 2000 statement totaling 52 paragraphs, and it was given over three days, the 17th, the 19th, and the 20th of April, 2008. Do you recall this statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes, I do. May I ask you a question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, you can't ask him a question. That's not permitted. Please be patient, just answer the questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can I ask now, this was a clarification of an approximately eight-page statement you'd given in 2002. Can you tell us, though, why it took three days to generate these clarifications?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, in the statements you indicated -- do you recall giving a statement in July of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that was to the Ministry of the Interior in Sarajevo. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'd like the court usher, please, to bring up 1D10-1570, which is the English version. B/C/S version is 1D10-1574. For the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Before your testimony today -- or have you been given an opportunity to review the 1992 statement? Ma'am, did you have an opportunity to review the 1992 statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so do you recall that in that statement you had never mentioned Milan Lukic, the Bikavac fire, the fact that you were present at that fire at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: I always mentioned, and I stand that -- and I stand by that, and I'm not afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, isn't it true that in the 1992 statement, the only time -- you never mentioned Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: He did the most evil. Him, Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, that wasn't the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Milan Lukic, Sredoje --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please just listen to me. The question that counsel is asking, counsel is saying that in your 1992 statement, you never mentioned Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw him in all the incidents, in every incident, and even if I didn't write that, I've come here to tell the truth, and I'm not afraid of doing so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, in your 2000 statement given to the Office of the Prosecutor for the ICTY, you indicated that Mitar Vasiljevic was the one that first arrested your husband. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: However, in your July 1992 statement, you indicated that your husband was arrested by Dragan Tomic while he was in the village of Prelovo trying to return home. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yet in your 2000 statement you indicate that Mitar Vasiljevic came in to your house to arrest him. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Yes. He was looking for him and went to Osavo [phoen] where he was, and Milan Lukic looked for me at Bikavac and Seganje and everywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But, ma'am, do you see the discrepancy? In one statement, the most recent after the incident, you state that your husband was arrested by the chief of police, Dragan Tomic, on his way back home from Prelovo, and in 2000, eight years later, you indicate that Mitar Vasiljevic arrested your husband after kicking in the door and demanding gold at your home. Can you explain that discrepancy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: You know what? If I -- if I didn't write in something, had you experienced and lived through what I had lived through, you wouldn't have been able to even write a third of what I've written.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, isn't it just true that you want revenge of the local Visegrad residents who you believe are responsible for these tragedies through hearsay and speaking with other people?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ossogo.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I disagree with this mischaracterisation of the client's motives saying that she wants revenge. I don't think this has any relevance to the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... that's my view, he's perfectly entitled to put it. And she can answer it. Are you here to get revenge, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: She has answered. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, in your 1992 statement you do indicate that there -- the Uzice Corps were doing the robbing. However, in the 1990 -- or excuse me, in the year 2000 statement you now name it as the locals Mitar Vasiljevic, Sredoje Lukic, Milan Lukic, and your neighbour. Who's that? What's his name, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: To answer your question, the Uzice Corps, the White Eagles, did not slaughter and kill people as much as these people did and slaughtered too. So I think that should now be clear to you, that everything's clear to you now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But I would put to you that in your 1992 statement you indicated that the Uzice Corps are the ones that came to your home looking for your husband and took away your television, video recorder, cassette player, kitchen knife, and gold jewellery, and that as they left they set fire to Kemal Hurem's shop and cafe and those belonging to Subasic and others.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: Not only Kemal Hurem's house but the whole hill was ablaze.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so what you're saying now is the Uzice Corps caused all that fire and destruction.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: I didn't even mention the Uzice Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: In 1992 you did.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-58
utterances.text: You know what? I don't want anybody to provoke me or me to provoke anyone. I come here to tell the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, there's a way in which you cross-examine when you are cross-examining on previous statements, which I think is not entirely satisfactory. You ask a question of the witness to indicate that the witness is not saying something that was in a previous statement, but you don't put the statement -- the statement is not put in evidence so that we can see it. It is left -- it is left hanging in the air.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, yes, Your Honour. When I ask that they be put up --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Excuse me. The statements are doing that same flashing thing that we were having trouble with the photograph on the e-court, and so I actually wanted to go paragraph by paragraph in a very controlled manner and do that for the Court, Your Honour, and of course I would be tendering the statements as evidence at the tail end of them, all the statements so the Court can do their own compare and contrast as to the changing statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But the proper way to do it, in my view, is to really put the statement in front of the witness and have the statement -- have the witness look at it and get her disagreement or agreement as to whether it bears out your proposition.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I agree with you completely, Your Honour. I'm just -- I'm kind of flustered by the e-court problems that we're having right now since they are blinking on and off. And, Your Honour, I'm not sure when the break is, but that would be essential to clear this problem up so the witness could see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The break is at 25 minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: There's a technical matter - well, I hope it's only technical - that I want to have clarified with the court deputy. Court deputy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, there is a technical problem. The statement on the e-court does not stay permanently, it blinks. It appears to be -- I don't have it. Yes, it doesn't stay on. It blinks.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might be of assistance to the Court. If Mr. Alarid tells us -- the witness can see it fine, it's just the rest of us who cannot. If Mr. Alarid gives us the reference, Mr. Van Hooydonk says that he's able to put it up on Sanction and I don't believe we have the same problem with Sanction, so as long as we have the reference, perhaps we can assist by putting it up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Another alternative the court deputy says is to go into private session and have it broadcast on the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: If I may assist, I can request from my assistant to prepare enough hard copies of all these statements, and that would be in ten minutes prepared. Ten or 15 minutes we can have all --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's very generous of you, but let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, before we can get into that as --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
